---
title: "Pol II pausing: example genes"
author: "Crystal Shan"
date: "`r Sys.Date()`"
output: html_document
---

Example genes for the Tullius et al. Figure 1F plots, chosen from the Day et al. 2016 pausing
index (`LCL_project/pausing/pause_index.tsv`, `code/pausing/cal_pausing_index/pause_index.R`).
Reads are read for each gene's TSS ± 1 kb when needed: fibertools nucleosome calls of the 31 LCL
samples (`ft extract --nuc`) and the FiberHMM combined 10–80 bp footprints. The selection
functions are in `pol2_functions.R`, the plot in `polII_pausing_plots.r`.

Outputs: `LCL_project/pausing/PolII/tables/example_genes.tsv` and
`LCL_project/pausing/PolII/plots/example_reads/<gene>.pdf`.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
source("/project/spott/cshan/fiber-seq/code/pausing/PolII/polII_pausing_plots.r")
```

## Inputs

The pausing-index table.

```{r inputs}
pi_tab <- fread(PI_TABLE)
pi_tab[analysis_set == TRUE,
       .(genes = .N, median_pi = median(pi), median_fpkm = median(fpkm)),
       keyby = .(pi_bin = factor(pi_bin, levels = PI_BINS))]
```

## Candidates

`example_candidates()`: analysis-set genes with no other gene's CAGE dominant TSS within
`OTHER_TSS_BP`; FPKM band = middle 50% of the analysis set; distance = |PI percentile − percentile
of the tertile median| + |FPKM percentile − 0.5|.

```{r candidates}
an <- example_candidates(pi_tab)
an[, .(genes = .N, candidates = sum(candidate), in_fpkm_band = sum(candidate & in_fpkm_band)),
   keyby = pi_bin]
```

## Examples per PI tertile

`pick_examples()`: per tertile, the first `N_EXAMPLES` candidates in the FPKM band, nearest the
target first, with at least `MIN_READS` fibers (`window_fiber_count()`: reads with an ft nucleosome
record in TSS ± 1 kb, counted only for the genes looked at).

```{r picks}
picks <- pick_examples(an)
picks[, .(group, gene_name, pi = signif(pi, 3), fpkm, n_reads, nearest_tss_bp,
          distance = round(distance, 3))]
```

## Positive control

`control_status()`: why each textbook paused gene (`CONTROL_GENES`) passes or fails (high
tertile, no other TSS within 1 kb, at least `MIN_READS` fibers); `add_control()` adds the
highest-PI one that passes.

```{r control}
controls <- control_status(pi_tab, an)
controls[, .(gene_name, chrom, pi = signif(pi, 3), fpkm, pi_bin, n_reads, status)]
picks <- add_control(picks, an, controls)
```

## Table

`write_example_table()`: `tables/example_genes.tsv`.

```{r table}
write_example_table(picks)
```

## Plots

`plot_tss_example()`: one PDF per gene in `plots/example_reads/`, centered on the gene's
FANTOM5 LCL dominant TSS (`fantom5.hg38.LCL.dominant_TSS.bed.gz`). Matching uses ENSG,
then gene symbol, on the same chromosome and strand; missing or ambiguous matches stop plotting.
30–<60 bp footprints containing a called sense GRO-seq peak are labeled PPP; 60–80 bp
footprints containing a called sense CAGE peak are labeled PIC. Other footprints in these
two size classes are gray and labeled unknown. Peak overlap means containing a called peak
base, not merely lying inside the peak-search window. GRO-seq peaks are searched at +20..+349 bp
and CAGE peaks at −50..+49 bp relative to the FANTOM5 TSS.
Example selection, the exported table's TSS, and pausing indices retain the original RefSeq
TSS definition; plotting rereads fibers and signals around the FANTOM5 TSS.

```{r plots}
for (g in picks$gene_name) plot_tss_example(g)
list.files(file.path(OUT_DIR, "plots/example_reads"))
```
